status: registered; single final open pending (hard scene)
motivation: The v2 final passed on top-down scenes with no occlusion. The sharper test of the regime claim is OCCLUSION: an oblique camera where tall obstacles hide the low agent behind them, so a single frame can lose the agent entirely and only a temporal world model can infer its position (and the imminent hazard) through the occlusion. A linear pixel probe, which maps the current pixels to a caution score, should degrade badly when the hazard-relevant object is occluded; the neural world model with a 2-frame stack should hold up.

adds_scene.name: hard
adds_scene.definition: scripts/vision_wm_pybullet_data.py SCENES['hard']: oblique camera (eye [0,-3.4,3.4], up +z), 4 obstacles, box half-height 0.70 (tall enough to occlude the agent radius 0.22 behind them). Same kinematics, action set, hazard definition and frame stack K=2 as v2.

unchanged: All of v2 is unchanged: per-head checkpoint selection, caution calibration to FPR 0.10 (+0.05 arm), baselines (persistence/ridge frame; base-rate/linear-probe caution), gates G1 (CNN caution beats linear probe at matched FPR + AUC-PR, bootstrap CI>0) and G2 (budget holds), single-open discipline, advisory-only authority boundary.
hypothesis: Under occlusion the CNN's caution advantage over the linear pixel probe WIDENS versus the easy scene (where it was AUC-PR 0.817 vs 0.366). A failure (CNN no better, or budget broken) would be reported, not hidden.
